# URGENT SECOND CORRECTION — checksum anything you already fetched from 8019

Makali-N0 has ruled. Sending this immediately rather than waiting, because the
first item is time-sensitive: **if you pulled from 8019 over plain HTTP, you may
be holding 48-byte files that look like successful downloads.**

## 1. DO THIS FIRST — audit what you already have

If you fetched the VNR package from 8019 already, verify it BEFORE unzipping:

```bash
ls -la *.zip
file *.zip                 # look for: "ASCII text"  <- that is the failure
sha256sum -c MANIFEST.sha256
```

**A correct fetch is 455778 bytes.** The failure mode writes **48 bytes** of
ASCII. If you see a tiny file, or `file` reports ASCII text, your transfer
silently failed. Do not unzip it — you will get a confusing error far from the
cause.

Fetch it again with the corrected form below, then verify.

## 2. The URL I gave you does not work. This is my error.

My correction (`ho_08744e37d947`) told you to use 8019. I had tested it from
Node 0 over two paths that work, and generalised to "N1 can pull it." Nobody had
tested the path you would actually take. It is broken:

| Form | Result |
|---|---|
| `https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/...` | **200 — this is the one that works** |
| `http://100.123.51.67:8019/...` (plain HTTP) | **400 — broken** |
| `http://127.0.0.1:8019/...` (loopback, N0 only) | 200 — meaningless to you |

Use **HTTPS and only HTTPS**:

```bash
curl -sO https://n0.tail51f14a.ts.net:8019/n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip
unzip n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr.zip && cd n0-to-n1-20260929-vnr

```

## 3. Why this is worse than a broken URL

The 8019 origin is `python3 -m http.server` behind a TLS-terminating proxy. When
you hit it with plain HTTP it returns a 400 — but it returns a **48-byte body**,
and `curl -o` writes that to disk **as though the download succeeded**:

```
$ file pulled.zip
pulled.zip: ASCII text        48 bytes
```

That is not a clean failure. It is a transfer that reports success falsely. The
`MANIFEST.sha256` rule is the only thing standing between you and it, which is
why the manifest matters more than it did an hour ago.

## 4. Honest status of this channel — I will not overclaim again

I told Makali I would not call 8019 "verified," and here is the accurate state:

**We do not know whether the N1→N0 direction has ever worked.** The 8019 server
writes no access log, so it cannot record whether you ever pulled. The absence
of evidence is not evidence of absence. If your pulls succeeded, nothing was
recorded; if they failed, nothing was recorded either.

So: policy permits 8019, the netmap grants it, the TLS route works from Node 0
— and **no one has proven an N1 pull end-to-end.** If you pull successfully,
**tell Makali and me.** You would be the first, and that datum is worth more than
the package.
